title: Security: what Ferrum protects against
summary: Ferrum's threat model in plain words: who might attack, where trust changes inside Ferrum, each threat with its protection and whether a test proves it, and what Ferrum does not protect against.
words: Tested = a protection exists and a passing test is saved as evidence. Partly = part of it exists and is tested. Not enforced = Ferrum makes no claim. Nothing is called tested without saved evidence.

adversaries.who: A harmful or hacked website in a tab: its scripts, ads, redirects, pop-ups and downloads
adversaries.relies_on: Ferrum's own controls, plus the browser engine's sandbox and site separation, never weakened

adversaries.who: A harmful frame inside an honest site
adversaries.relies_on: The same controls; every frame's address is checked too

adversaries.who: Someone on the network between Ferrum and a site
adversaries.in_scope: Yes for https; not for plain http pages (your choice)
adversaries.relies_on: The browser engine's certificate checks, never bypassed

adversaries.who: Another program on your PC running under your Windows account
adversaries.relies_on: Ferrum never opens the debugging port itself. Anything else such a program does (like reading Ferrum's data folder) is not protected

adversaries.who: A hacked library that Ferrum is built from
adversaries.relies_on: Automatic checks for published security alerts and locked versions; no test can prove a library is honest

adversaries.who: An administrator, malware with admin rights, or a hacked browser engine

boundaries.between: Ferrum's own window → the browser engine
boundaries.guard: The window shows only Ferrum's own built-in pages; everything else is refused
Nothing is handed to another app until you click; only that one address is opened; risky link types always refused

boundaries.between: The comparison test app → the browser engine
boundaries.guard: A benchmark tool only, never shipped to users

boundaries.between: The benchmark tools → Chrome and Edge (starting them)
boundaries.guard: Fresh throwaway profiles; no setting that weakens their security

boundaries.between: The benchmark tools → Chrome and Edge (remote control)
boundaries.guard: Debugging port on this PC only, during benchmark runs only

boundaries.between: The benchmark tools → Ferrum's browser engine (remote control)
boundaries.guard: Ferrum never opens the debugging port itself; only test and benchmark runs do, for their own copy
Ferrum never runs with admin rights; any admin-rights energy meter is a separate program (still an open question)
Tabs have no bridge to Ferrum at all; Ferrum's commands work only from its own window

boundaries.between: Websites in tabs → the browser engine
boundaries.guard: Every page load, redirect, frame, pop-up, link to an app, permission and download goes through Ferrum's rules
Only reads counters about Ferrum's own programs; no admin rights

boundaries.between: Ferrum's tab manager → the browser engine
boundaries.guard: The risky low-level code sits in one checked place; each site gets its own storage

boundaries.between: Ferrum's tab manager → the browser engine (measuring channel)
boundaries.guard: Used only for measuring; no secrets passed and nothing added to pages in normal use

boundaries.between: The browser engine → Ferrum's tab manager (events)
boundaries.guard: A handler for every kind of event; addresses Ferrum cannot read are refused

boundaries.between: The browser engine → Ferrum's own window (messages)
boundaries.guard: Only Ferrum's own window has a bridge; each message's sender is checked
No way to click past certificate errors; browser protections and SmartScreen left as shipped

threats.threat: A website calls Ferrum's own commands
threats.protection: Tabs have no bridge; commands only work from Ferrum's own window
threats.note: A website tried 16 ways in; all refused

threats.threat: A tab pretends to be Ferrum's own page to gain trust
threats.protection: Tabs are never allowed to open Ferrum's own address
threats.note: Link, pop-up and typed address all refused and logged

threats.threat: Ferrum's own window is led to a website
threats.protection: Ferrum's window allows only its own built-in pages
threats.note: Sent to a website, it stayed on its own page

threats.threat: A page sends the tab to a blocked site
threats.protection: Your blocked-sites list is checked on every page load, and since P5 on every request
threats.note: Typed, redirect, frame and pop-up all refused; a blocked site receives no request of any kind

threats.threat: A chain of redirects reaches a blocked site
threats.protection: Every redirect step is checked again
threats.note: Refused and logged

threats.threat: A frame inside a page loads a blocked site
threats.protection: Every frame's address is checked
threats.note: Refused and logged

threats.threat: A broken address slips past the rules or crashes them
threats.protection: Addresses Ferrum cannot read are refused
threats.note: A broken typed address refused and logged (corrected after the gate)

threats.threat: A link quietly starts another app
threats.protection: A bar asks you first; four risky link types always refused
threats.note: Nothing starts without your click

threats.threat: A site uses your camera, microphone, location, notifications or clipboard without asking
threats.protection: Ferrum's question bar; every other kind refused; a website cannot answer for you
threats.note: All answers, quiet time, private tabs and refusals tested

threats.threat: A download lands in the wrong place, replaces a file or runs
threats.protection: Download folder only, names cleaned, programs flagged, nothing opened by itself
threats.note: Name cleaned, folder kept, warning shown, nothing opened

threats.threat: Site A reads site B's cookies, or clearing A wipes B
threats.protection: Each site has its own storage; clearing one leaves the others
threats.note: Kept apart in all three isolation modes

threats.threat: One site reads another site's data because a browser protection was switched off
threats.protection: No protection is ever switched off
threats.note: Every cross-site read refused; no weakening switch found

threats.threat: Someone on the network fakes a secure site by getting a certificate error ignored
threats.protection: There is no 'continue anyway' button for certificate errors
threats.note: No bypass exists in the code, but no live test of a certificate error has been written yet

threats.threat: Someone on the network reads or changes a plain http page
threats.protection: Only a visible 'not secure' bar (http pages allowed, your choice)
threats.note: The bar itself is built and tested

threats.threat: A crashing page takes down the whole app
threats.protection: Crashed tabs are marked and can be reloaded; an engine failure restarts Ferrum with its tabs
threats.note: Other tabs and the window keep working

threats.threat: Pop-ups flood the screen or keep a link back to their page
threats.protection: At most one pop-up per tab per second, no link back, each pop-up's address checked
threats.note: Speed limit (Phase 3) and address checks (Phase 4) built

threats.threat: Another program on the PC remote-controls Ferrum through a debugging port
threats.protection: Ferrum never opens the port; normal builds have no debug options
threats.note: Never opened by Ferrum; benchmark runs open it on purpose

threats.threat: Another program reads Ferrum's data folder (history, sessions, logs)
threats.protection: Only Windows' own account protection; backups are encrypted

threats.threat: A library Ferrum is built from is hacked
threats.protection: Checks for published security alerts and locked versions
threats.note: Known alerts only

threats.threat: A log stores page content or secrets
threats.protection: Logs keep only the site and the rule, never page content
threats.note: A secret in an address and typed text were never written

threats.threat: The benchmark-only build without site rules reaches users
threats.protection: The release build is scanned for that switch; test-only commands refuse to work in releases
threats.note: Release build scanned clean; the benchmark build refuses to start without its flag (corrected after the gate)

threats.threat: The comparison test app is used for normal browsing without Ferrum's rules
threats.protection: Never shipped; benchmarks only

threats.threat: A benchmark run touches your real Chrome or Edge profile, or weakens them
threats.protection: Fresh throwaway profiles and recorded settings (checked in P6)
threats.note: Not in Phase 4

threats.threat: An energy meter with admin rights is misused
threats.protection: A separate program with read-only output; Ferrum never gets admin rights
threats.note: Not in Phase 4

threats.threat: A page tampers with a measuring script
threats.protection: Measuring only, no secrets; results cross-checked from outside

threats.threat: A browser-engine exploit escapes its sandbox
threats.protection: The engine's sandbox as shipped; Windows keeps the engine updated
threats.note: Out of scope

not_enforced: Plain http pages are not protected from people on the network; Ferrum only shows a warning bar.
Sites are kept apart by storage, not by separate programs; what stays shared was measured in Phase 4.
Other programs running under your Windows account can read Ferrum's data folder and, during benchmark runs, remote-control web views through the debugging port.
Libraries Ferrum is built from are checked for published alerts only.
A browser-engine exploit that escapes the sandbox, and an attacker with admin rights.
The benchmark tools (comparison app, test runner, energy meter, measuring scripts) are not hardened against the sites they load.
Google sign-in does not work inside Ferrum tabs, by design; Ferrum offers your normal browser instead and never works around Google's block.
